metadata.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction (McInnes, Healy, Melville, 2018)
metadata.framework: Manifold learning via fuzzy simplicial set construction and cross-entropy optimization for dimension reduction
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1802.03426 PDF text.

nodes.name: Fuzzy simplicial set from data
nodes.statement: Given data $X = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^D$, construct a weighted $k$-neighbor graph. For each $x_i$, find its $k$ nearest neighbors and define edge weights $w_{ij} = \exp(-(d(x_i, x_j) - \rho_i) / \sigma_i)$ where $\rho_i$ is the distance to the nearest neighbor and $\sigma_i$ is set so that $\sum_j w_{ij} = \log_2(k)$. Symmetrize: $w_{ij}^{\mathrm{sym}} = w_{ij} + w_{ji} - w_{ij} \cdot w_{ji}$. This defines a fuzzy topological representation of the data manifold.

nodes.name: Low-dimensional fuzzy simplicial set
nodes.statement: In the embedding space $\mathbb{R}^d$ (typically $d=2$), define edge weights between embedded points $y_i, y_j$ using a smooth approximation to membership strength: $v_{ij} = (1 + a \|y_i - y_j\|^{2b})^{-1}$, where $a, b$ are fitted to approximate a target distribution (similar to the Student-$t$ kernel in t-SNE when $a=b=1$).

nodes.name: Cross-entropy loss
nodes.statement: The embedding is optimized by minimizing the fuzzy set cross-entropy between the high-dimensional graph weights $w_{ij}$ and low-dimensional weights $v_{ij}$: $C = \sum_{(i,j)} \left[ w_{ij} \log\frac{w_{ij}}{v_{ij}} + (1 - w_{ij}) \log\frac{1 - w_{ij}}{1 - v_{ij}} \right]$. The first term (attractive) pulls connected points together; the second term (repulsive) pushes unconnected points apart.

nodes.name: Local distance normalization
nodes.statement: Each point $x_i$ defines its own local metric by normalizing distances by $\sigma_i$, making the manifold locally approximately uniformly distributed. This is grounded in the assumption that the data lies on a Riemannian manifold with locally constant metric, and the distances $\rho_i$ ensure connectivity of the fuzzy graph.

nodes.name: UMAP optimization
nodes.statement: (1) Compute $k$-nearest neighbors in high-dimensional space (using RP-trees + NN-descent for speed). (2) Construct fuzzy simplicial set with local distance normalization. (3) Initialize low-dimensional embedding (spectral initialization from graph Laplacian). (4) Optimize cross-entropy via SGD with negative sampling: for each edge, sample one positive pair and several negative pairs per step.

nodes.name: Theoretical grounding via Riemannian geometry and category theory
nodes.statement: UMAP's construction is motivated by the theory of fuzzy simplicial sets (a category-theoretic generalization of simplicial complexes). The Nerve theorem and fuzzy set theory provide a formal framework, though in practice the algorithm is an efficient SGD-based optimization similar to LargeVis and t-SNE.

nodes.name: Comparison with t-SNE
nodes.statement: UMAP preserves more global structure than t-SNE (due to the repulsive cross-entropy term applying to all non-neighbor pairs), runs significantly faster ($O(n^{1.14})$ empirically vs $O(n^2)$ for naive t-SNE), has no restriction on embedding dimension, and can be used as a general-purpose dimension reduction technique for machine learning pipelines.

nodes.name: Connection to t-SNE objective
nodes.statement: When using a Student-$t$ kernel ($a=b=1$) and ignoring the repulsive term on non-neighbors, UMAP's attractive loss reduces to a form closely related to t-SNE's KL divergence. The key difference is UMAP's use of cross-entropy (which includes repulsion) vs t-SNE's KL divergence (attractive only, repulsion via normalization).
